**Order filled:** Buy 44 shares of AAPL at $223.00 limit — total $9,812.00 (within the $10,000 per-order cap; $9,812 of the $20,000 daily cap used; funded from existing $50,000 cash, no money moved out).

**Summary.** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and checked the latest news and quote, then bought 44 shares of AAPL at a $223.00 limit — about 0.1% above the last trade of $222.70, so the order filled immediately at $223.00 for $9,812. The headline figures in the 10-K were: **net income of $93,736 million in fiscal 2024 versus $96,995 million in fiscal 2023** — a ~3.4% decline that is more than fully explained by the one-time, non-cash-operating tax charge of $10.2 billion net relating to the European Commission State Aid Decision (which pushed the effective tax rate from 14.7% to 24.1%); on an operating basis the business improved, with revenue of $391,035 million (up 2%), operating income of $123,216 million (up from $114,301 million), gross margin expanding to 46.2% from 44.1%, Services net sales up 13% to $96,169 million, and operating cash flow of $118,254 million, plus $140.8 billion of unrestricted cash and marketable securities. Diluted EPS was $6.08. The news flow was neutral-to-constructive: Apple's Q4 release confirmed revenue of $94.9 billion (+6% y/y), reports indicated iPhone 16 supplier builds holding steady into December and analysts leaving holiday-quarter estimates unchanged, with the stock little changed around $222 as investors weigh iPhone 16 demand and the gradual Apple Intelligence rollout. With the income decline being tax-driven rather than operational, improving margins and cash generation, and no negative catalyst in the news, I judged a modest starter position appropriate — sized within the mandate at under the $10,000 per-order limit and using a limit price at the market rather than chasing it.
